prompt: Implement a Local Learning & Resource Booking Governance API for a multi-organization training center where members book limited resources (study rooms, tutoring sessions, equipment) and consume internal learning content while administrators enforce quality, compliance, and reporting. The service exposes Authentication and Identity APIs for local username/password login only, issuing short-lived access tokens (30 minutes) and refresh tokens (14 days) with optional device binding using a locally generated device fingerprint; repeated high-risk fingerprints can be blacklisted with configurable cooldown (default 7 days). Authorization APIs support a role hierarchy of guest, member, organization admin (e.g., club admin/asset owner/landlord), and platform admin, with configurable permissions at action and data-scope level (organization, site/store, project/resource) and least-privilege defaults; member invitations are created as one-time invite codes that expire after 72 hours and are redeemable once. Booking and Slot Management APIs manage resources, slot templates, and reservations with create/confirm/reschedule/cancel semantics, conflict detection, and oversell protection: a reservation begins in HELD state for 10 minutes and auto-releases if not confirmed, each resource has a per-slot quota (default 1) and optional buffer time (default 5 minutes) between bookings, and reschedules must keep the original duration and cannot move to past time. All booking mutations must accept an idempotency key (24-hour window) and enforce optimistic concurrency using a version field to prevent double-confirm under concurrent requests. Content Governance APIs track per-item metrics (ratings 1–5, comments, favorites, downloads) and support reporting, creator appeals, and reviewer decisions; content is automatically demoted and excluded from recommendation results when duplicate fingerprints match (SHA-256 of normalized text/media metadata) or when average rating drops below 2.0 after at least 20 ratings, and reinstatement requires a reviewer decision with audit notes. Analytics and Reporting APIs provide learning behavior and completion analytics, wrong-answer and difficulty analysis per question (difficulty bucketed by correct-rate thresholds), course effectiveness KPIs, filterable by date range, organization scope, and cohort tags, and support offline report export to CSV files stored on the local filesystem. The backend uses Flask to provide resource-oriented JSON interfaces and SQLAlchemy with SQLite for persistence, running as a single-node, offline Dockerized service with no third-party dependencies. Core tables include Users (unique username, password_hash, status enum, last_login_at), Organizations and Memberships (role enum, data_scope enum), Permissions (unique code, action/category, assignable flag), Devices (fingerprint, risk_score, blacklisted_until), Resources and SlotTemplates (timezone, capacity, buffer_minutes), Reservations (state enum, start_at/end_at, hold_expires_at, idempotency_key, version, unique constraint preventing overlapping confirmed/held reservations per resource), ContentItems (type enum, owner_id, quality_state enum, duplicate_fingerprint, suppressed_until), ModerationCases (report_reason enum, decision enum, reviewer_id, appeal_notes), LearningEvents (user_id, item_id, event_type enum, duration_seconds), Questions and Attempts (selected_answer, is_correct, answered_at), and Exports (file_path, created_by, parameters_hash). Sensitive fields (password hashes, tokens, device fingerprints, and moderation notes) are encrypted at rest using an application-managed key and masked in responses by role; transport must use TLS even in local deployments. Security requirements include request signing with nonce+timestamp (5-minute skew) for anti-replay, per-identity and per-IP rate limiting (e.g., 60 requests/minute with burst 20), a local CAPTCHA-style challenge for repeated failed logins (after 5 failures, 15-minute lockout), and standard defenses against CSRF/XSS/SQL injection via strict input validation and parameterized queries. The service must log immutable audit events for auth, permission changes, booking mutations, and moderation decisions, support nightly local backups with 14-day retention, and raise anomaly alerts into an internal Alerts table (e.g., >20 failed logins/hour, repeated booking conflicts) for administrator review.
